messages:
Nina: Opening thread for a new dedicated-capacity idea: Dynamic Surge Policy (DSP). Goal: let customers buy a baseline reserved pool + a predictable surge contract that controls autoscale behavior and billing.
Ravi: can you sketch constraints? e.g. surge_budget per-day, per-route caps, and a billing multiplier?
Nina: yes. sketch: surge_budget = X tokens/day, surge_multiplier controls price for overage, and admission_policy decides if surge triggers autoscale vs queue.
Emma: product ask: expose policy templates (standard, conservative, aggressive) so customers pick tradeoffs without fiddling with knobs. templates include guardrails for preemption and latency targets.
Zoe: runtime matter: DSP needs new admission path to annotate requests with surge_eligibility and an admission token. autoscaler should consult surge_token_count to avoid scaling for ephemeral spikes.
Ravi: billing: charge baseline monthly commit; surge usage billed with surge_multiplier and show projected monthly spend. FinanceBot: can we model sample invoices for multiplier 3x?
FinanceBot: sample (mock): reserved 10k tokens/min commit -> $4,000/mo; surge_used 12k tokens -> $0.012/token * 3x = $432. Totals for month = $4,432. (mock numbers)
Emma: launch scope MVP: API to set DSP template, dashboard showing surge meter, server-side admission check, billing line item. Exclude automated recovery/rollback.
Zoe: autoscale interaction: propose hysteresis 5m for surge-driven scale-ups to avoid flip-flopping, and a cap_percent so surge cannot consume >30% of regional spare capacity.
Nina: negotiation point for customers: allow opt-in flexible vs locked surge. locked = reserved min guarantee for the surge window (higher price). flexible = no guarantee but cheaper.
Ravi: legal ask: contract language for surge SLAs and refund policy if we fail to provide surge capacity. Emma: we'll draft pilot T&Cs.
Zoe: telemetry tag `dsp_v1` and audit logs for surge grants. OpsBot: staging run shows DSP admission endpoint passes basic tests.
Nina: launch criteria draft: (1) API stable, (2) dashboard meter + billing sample, (3) autoscale hysteresis implemented in canary, (4) docs + pilot T&Cs, (5) ops runbook.
Emma: Sales ask: Pilot customers want 1-min burst guarantees for webhook routes. can MVP support 60s windows?
Zoe: yes but recommend conservative defaults: max_tokens_per_min default 5k and require ops review for >10k.
Ravi: action items: Zoe -> implement admission + telemetry PR, Emma -> pilot T&Cs and templates, Nina -> RFC and roadmap card, FinanceBot -> invoice export for pilots.
OpsBot: canary scheduled 2026-06-02T16:00Z.
Nina: thumbs up. if no blocks we'll add to Q3 roadmap and schedule customer briefings.
